skill.name: Fresh or tired: swap a cliché for a fresh image
skill.why: Readers skip comparisons they've heard before. Fresh ones make them see your scene.
skill.how: Spot the comparison you've heard a hundred times. Swap in one that fits your details.

steps.say: Here's the first line of my footy report. It was freezing at the ground.
show: At the footy, my feet were
steps.ask: Where else do people say as cold as ice?

options.text: about almost anything cold: hands, drinks, wind
only about real ice cubes
options.reason: People say it about cold hands and cold drinks too. It's not about ice.

options.text: only at the footy
options.reason: There's no ice at the footy. People say it everywhere, about anything.

steps.win: Yes! It's a set saying, used for anything cold. It's been said so often it's worn out.

steps.say: A worn-out comparison like that is called a cliché. Readers skip right past it.

show.text: as quiet as an empty classroom
show.nudge: That's a new picture. You can see the empty desks.

show.text: as quiet as socks on carpet
show.nudge: That's new too. It isn't a set saying.

steps.win: Yes! People say quiet as a mouse about anything. The others are new, so they're fresh.

steps.say: Let's swap my cliché. The best fresh picture comes from inside the scene.
show: my feet were as cold as ...
steps.ask: Which fresh picture comes from the footy?

options.text: as cold as a penguin's toes
options.reason: That's fresh, but there are no penguins at the footy. Look around the ground.

options.text: as cold as the metal seats in the stand
as cold as ice
options.reason: That's the cliché we're swapping out.

steps.win: Yes! I'm sitting on those cold metal seats. The picture comes from inside the scene.

steps.say: Careful! Being in the scene isn't enough. The picture has to fit the detail too.
show: the sand was as hot as ...
steps.ask: Which picture is in the scene AND fits?

options.text: the cold drinks in the esky
options.reason: The esky is at the beach, but cold drinks aren't hot! It has to fit.

options.text: a volcano in a movie
options.reason: That's hot, but there's no volcano at the beach. Look around the scene.

options.text: the barbecue plate beside us

steps.win: Yes! The barbecue plate is at the beach, and it's hot. It's in the scene, and it fits.

steps.say: Some idioms are clichés too. They're fine when you talk. In a story, a fresh picture works harder.

show.text: The queue curled round the canteen like a sleepy python.
show.nudge: That's a new picture, made for this scene. Look for a set saying.

show.text: Mo took to cooking like a duck to water.
His pancakes flopped like wet beach towels.
show.nudge: That's a new picture too. Look for a set saying.

steps.win: Yes! Like a duck to water is an idiom and a cliché. Fresh pictures make readers look.

terms.means: A set saying used so often it's worn out. Readers skip past it.
A new picture, made for this scene, that fits its details.
Where you are and what's around you. Find your picture there.

examples.text: as cold as the metal seats in the stand.

card.test: Is it a set saying? Swap in a picture from the scene that fits the details.

creature.name: Swishbill
creature.blurb: A royal spoonbill that sweeps its bill through the mangrove mud. It spits out tired old sayings and gulps down fresh pictures that fit.

encounters.frame: The Swishbill is sweeping through Wren's wildlife diary, looking for something tired.
encounters.text: Wren's diary, Monday. Today I met Lulu, a baby wombat. She is round and fluffy. Her fur is as soft as a new paintbrush. She waddles everywhere, and she loves carrots. When she is asleep, she is as quiet as a mouse. Then she starts to snore. Her snores sound like a tiny lawnmower. Mo says she snores better than he does.
encounters.prompt: Which comparison in Wren's diary is a cliché?
encounters.success: As quiet as a mouse. People say it all the time, so it's worn out.

options.text: as soft as a new paintbrush
options.reason: This one is fresh. You don't hear it every day.

options.text: as quiet as a mouse
like a tiny lawnmower
options.reason: This one is fresh. It's a new, funny picture of a wombat snoring.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing back to Mo from a space station. The Swishbill is reading over his shoulder.
encounters.text: Zed was spending a week on the Starhopper space station. At night, the crew slept in sleeping bags strapped to the wall. The lights were turned down low. Outside the window, the stars didn't twinkle. They just shone. The only sound was the soft hum of the air fan. Zed floated by the window, writing in his diary. Mo had sent him a message: 'Bet you're sleeping like a log up there!'
encounters.prompt: Mo used a cliché. Which fresh picture fits how the crew sleeps on the station?
encounters.success: Sleeping bags strapped to a wall hang there just like coats on hooks.

options.text: like coats hung up on hooks
like a log
options.reason: That's the cliché Mo used. Readers have heard it far too often.

options.text: like a cat curled up on a couch
options.reason: There are no couches up there. The crew sleep in bags strapped to the wall.

encounters.frame: Mo is writing a postcard to his nan. The Swishbill spotted a tired comparison.
encounters.text: Dear Nan, today the crew went snorkelling off the far end of Mirage Mangroves. I wore the flippers you gave me, and I only fell over twice. The water was as clear as crystal. We could see the sandy bottom five metres down, and I could count the stripes on every single fish. A school of tiny blue ones swam right past my mask, so close I could see their eyes. Wren found a sea star and let me hold it. Indi drew it on her waterproof notepad. Gus said the water was perfect for science. I said it was perfect for lunch. Love, Mo
encounters.prompt: 'As clear as crystal' is a cliché. Which fresh picture fits Mo's snorkelling trip?
encounters.success: You can see every fish in a clean fish tank, just like Mo counting the stripes.

options.text: as clear as a puddle on the oval after training
options.reason: Puddles after training are brown and muddy. Mo can count every stripe on every fish.

options.text: as clear as mud
options.reason: That's another cliché, and it means not clear at all. Mo can see five metres down.

options.text: as clear as the glass of a clean fish tank

encounters.frame: Indi's art class painted at the mangroves. The Swishbill is checking their notes for tired comparisons.
encounters.text: On Thursday, Indi's art class took their easels down to the mangroves. The afternoon light was soft and golden. The water was as smooth as a fresh sheet of paper. Indi painted the sunset. When Ms Rao saw it, she said it looked like a million dollars. Indi was pleased, but secretly she thought it looked a bit like a squashed mango. Wren painted a heron that stood on one leg like a coat hanger with feathers. Gus didn't paint at all. He collected mud samples. Mo painted a fish. At least, he said it was a fish. Everyone else thought it was a sausage.

encounters.frame: Mo is writing a Field Guide entry about a tawny frogmouth. The Swishbill thinks he can do better.
encounters.text: Field Guide entry: Tawny frogmouth. We found this bird on our second night at Mirage Mangroves. Wren spotted it first, which is lucky, because nobody else could see it at all. It was perched at the end of a broken branch, with its eyes squeezed shut and its beak pointing up at the sky. Its feathers were grey and streaky, exactly like the bark around it. For nearly an hour, it didn't move a single feather, even when a mozzie landed on its head. Mo held the torch while Wren took notes. Gus said it was pretending to be part of the tree, so that owls and snakes wouldn't notice it. Frogmouths are not owls, even though everyone thinks they are. At midnight, it finally opened one yellow eye, snapped up a moth and went straight back to being a branch. In my notes I wrote that it was as still as a statue. Wren says I can do better than that.
encounters.prompt: 'As still as a statue' is a cliché. Which fresh picture fits this frogmouth?
encounters.success: The frogmouth is pretending to be part of that broken branch, so the picture fits exactly.

options.text: as still as a kid on the last day of term
options.reason: Kids on the last day of term can't sit still. This bird doesn't move a feather.

options.text: as still as the broken branch it was perched on
as still as a statue
options.reason: That's the cliché Mo wrote. Wren wants something fresher.

options.text: as still as a goldfish darting round its bowl
options.reason: A darting goldfish never stops moving. The frogmouth stays still for an hour.

encounters.frame: Gus wrote a report on his robot's first race. The Swishbill is hunting for the tired line.
encounters.text: Robot Race Report, by Gus. Bolt lined up on the start line next to six other robots. There were prizes for first, second and third, and a special prize for any robot that didn't explode. The crowd was mostly parents and one very excited dog. Its silver arms swung like a gate in a gale as it warmed up, and its wheels were as quiet as a fridge at midnight. When the flag dropped, the robot next to Bolt fell over, and two others crashed into each other. Bolt didn't even flinch. It shot past them like greased lightning. At the halfway mark, it beeped like a supermarket checkout to tell me it was low on battery. I had forgotten to charge it. Bolt still came second, and it only stopped once to make toast. I am very proud of it. Next year, I am charging it the night before.
encounters.prompt: Which comparison in Gus's report is a cliché?
encounters.success: Like greased lightning. People have said it so many times that it's worn out.

encounters.frame: Indi is writing a spooky story about the old boatshed. The Swishbill wants her to swap out a tired comparison.
encounters.text: Under the old boatshed at Crooked Creek there is a cellar that nobody has opened for fifty years. Nobody in town will say why. It smells of rope, salt and old fishing nets. The walls are lined with rusty hooks and tackle boxes, and the floor is covered in dried-up bait. On Saturday, Indi and Zed lifted the trapdoor and shone their torch down the ladder. Indi's torch flickered twice. The beam only reached the third rung. Zed said he could hear dripping, but he couldn't tell where it was coming from. Below that, there was nothing to see at all. They decided to come back another day, with a much bigger torch. Indi wrote the whole thing down as soon as they got back to the boat. In her first draft, Indi wrote that the cellar was as dark as night. Zed said that was a cliché, and that she should use something from the boatshed instead.
encounters.prompt: Which fresh picture from the boatshed fits Indi's cellar?
encounters.success: A shut tackle box is pitch-dark inside, and tackle boxes line the cellar walls.

options.text: as dark as the inside of a shut tackle box
as black as coal
options.reason: That's another cliché, and Zed wants something from the boatshed.

options.text: as dark as a cinema before the film starts
options.reason: A cinema is dark, but it isn't in the boatshed. Zed asked for something from there.

options.text: as dark as a beach at lunchtime in summer
options.reason: A summer beach at lunchtime is blazing with light, and it isn't in the boatshed.

encounters.frame: Tully is writing up last night's storm in the ship's log. The Swishbill is perched on her pencil.
encounters.text: By midnight, the storm had turned the bay into something none of the crew had seen before. The Soggy Biscuit climbed each wave slowly, groaning, until it hung at the very top for one horrible second, and then it plunged down the other side so fast that Mo's saucepans flew off their hooks. From the deck, Tully could see the tip of the mast against the lightning. Every wave that rolled towards them was taller than the mast itself, a black wall of water with white foam spilling off its top. The rain came sideways and stung their faces. Zed had tied himself to the wheel with a skipping rope. Indi gave up on her sketchbook after the third page blew away. Wren had wrapped the Creatures in towels and wedged them into the bunks. Gus was being sick into a bucket, which he said was a perfectly normal scientific reaction. Nobody slept. In the morning, when the sea was flat again and everyone was eating dry toast, Tully wrote up the night in the ship's log. Her first sentence said that the waves had been as big as houses. She crossed it out, chewed her pencil, and looked up at the mast.
encounters.prompt: Tully crossed out a cliché. Which fresh picture comes from what she saw that night?
encounters.success: Tully watched every wave rise higher than the mast, so a picture built on the mast fits exactly.

options.text: waves as tall as a stack of breakfast pancakes
options.reason: A stack of pancakes is small. These waves were taller than the mast.

options.text: waves as big as houses
options.reason: That's the cliché Tully crossed out. Readers have heard it many times.

options.text: waves as tall as the Soggy Biscuit's own mast
waves as tall as the lighthouse on Pelican Point
options.reason: That's fresh, but there's no lighthouse in Tully's night. She was looking up at the mast.

parts: At low tide, the water drains out of Mirage Mangroves and leaves behind a mudflat that stretches almost to the horizon. Indi went out at sunrise with her sketchbook and a pencil, determined to draw it before the tide came back. The air smelled of salt and rotten eggs. She had borrowed Mo's gumboots, which were three sizes too big, and twice she nearly lost one in the mud.

parts.tap: The mangrove roots poked up out of the mud like the bristles of an old toothbrush.
parts.reason: This one is fresh. An old toothbrush is a new picture for the roots.

parts: She had drawn the mangroves a hundred times before, but she had never noticed how much the mud looked like her own sketchbook paper: grey, smooth and waiting for someone to make a mark on it. By the time the tide came back, she had filled six pages. Her sneakers were never the same again.

encounters.frame: The crew is watching Maxx Vantablack's live stream from the Vantadome. The Swishbill's bill is twitching.
encounters.text: 'Maxx it out, Vantafam!' The live stream opened on Maxx Vantablack standing on the top deck of the Vantadome, with the glass dome glittering behind him and the waterslide curling off the back like a gold ribbon. Behind him, two Goldies in gold tracksuits held up a banner that said RESCUE SANCTUARY in glitter. Thirty-eight million people were watching. He flashed a smile so white that viewers all over the world reached for their sunnies. His silver hair had been sprayed into a wave as stiff as a frozen ocean, and it didn't move once, even when a seagull landed on it. 'Today,' he purred, in a voice as smooth as a gold jet ski gliding over a glassy bay, 'I unveil my brand-new Creature Rescue Sanctuary.' The MaxxCam drone swung around to show a row of very small cages. 'They'll be as snug as a bug in a rug in there,' he added, patting the bars. Something inside one of the cages whimpered. Maxx turned up the music. Comments poured in, mostly hearts. 'Smash that heart button like it owes you money!' On the Soggy Biscuit, Wren switched off the screen without a word. Gus wrote down the time, Zed took a screenshot, and Indi started sketching every cage.
encounters.prompt: Which comparison in Maxx's stream is a cliché?
encounters.success: As snug as a bug in a rug. It's so worn out that nobody stops to picture those tiny cages.

encounters.frame: Wren is writing about the morning the fog came in. The Swishbill wants her to swap out a tired comparison.
encounters.text: On the crew's fourth morning at Mirage Mangroves, they woke to find that the island had disappeared. A fog had rolled in overnight, so thick and white that from the deck of the Soggy Biscuit you couldn't see the end of the gangplank. Mo was standing at the little stove on deck, stirring a pot of porridge so thick that the spoon stood up by itself. Every so often it gave a slow, heavy bloop. Wren and Zed set off along the boardwalk to check on the Creatures. After ten steps, the boat behind them had vanished. After twenty, they could barely see each other's faces, and the only way to stay on the boardwalk was to keep one hand on the rail. Even the birds had gone quiet. Wren called out, and her voice sounded small and flat. Somewhere close by, something splashed. It turned out to be the Swishbill, fishing for breakfast. Neither of them said much on the way back. Back on board, Wren started writing about it in her diary. Her first sentence said the fog was as thick as pea soup. Indi read it over her shoulder and said, 'That's a cliché. Use something from this morning instead.' Wren looked across the deck at Mo's stove.
encounters.prompt: Which fresh picture fits the fog Wren is writing about?
encounters.success: The fog was so thick they couldn't see, and Mo's porridge was thick enough to hold up a spoon.

options.reason: That's the cliché Wren wrote first. Indi asked for something from this morning.

options.reason: That's a cliché about close friends, not about fog.

options.text: as thin as the steam from a cup of tea
options.reason: Steam is thin and see-through. This fog hid the end of the gangplank.
